:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
The area of ​​the triangle $\triangle ABC$ is $24\sqrt{2} \text{ cm}^2.$ Find $AB.$

![](images/e9/e93e732bd04cfda304c2098087548a638d8d869ccf8b1050235e8207825875d3.png)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
\mathcal{A}=\dfrac{1}{2}bc\sin{A},
$$

where $\angle{A}$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB, \\ b & =AC=12\text{ cm}, \\ m∠A & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\sin{45^{\circ}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $c=AB,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 24\sqrt{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 12\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\ 24\sqrt{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 12\cdot c\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\ 24\cancel{\sqrt{2}} & =3\cancel{\sqrt{2}}c \\ 24 & =3c \\ c & =8\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AB = 8\,\textrm{cm}.$

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $5\sqrt{3}\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.$ Find $AC.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=5\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 5\sqrt{3} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\ 5\sqrt{3} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 5\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\ 5\sqrt{3} & =\frac{5\sqrt{3}\,b}{4} \\ \cancel{5\sqrt{3}} & =\frac{\cancel{5\sqrt{3}}\,b}{4} \\ 1 & =\frac{b}{4} \\ b & =4\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=4\,\text{cm}.$

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2}{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Find $AC.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=6\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 6\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 6\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}\,b}{2} \\ \frac{21\cancel{\sqrt{2}}}{\cancel{2}} & =\frac{3\cancel{\sqrt{2}}\,b}{\cancel{2}} \\ 3b & =21 \\ b & =7\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=7\,\text{cm}.$

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2}{\text{cm}}^{2}.$ Then,  $AC=${{field-1}} $\text{cm}.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=10\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={120}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 10\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\ \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 10\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\ \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2} & =5b\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ 25\cancel{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} & =5b\cdot \cancel{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \\ 5b & =25 \\ b & =5\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}

The area of ​​the acute triangle $△ABC$ is $3{\text{ mm}}^{2}.$ Then, the measure of $∠A$ is{{field-1}} ${}^{∘}.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=\sqrt{3}\,\text{ mm}, \\ b & =AC=4\,\text{mm}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $m∠A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot \sqrt{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 3 & =2\sqrt{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡A & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ m∠A & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the acute triangle $△ABC$ is $20\sqrt{2}{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Then, the measure of $∠A$ is{{field-1}} ${}^{∘}.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=8\,\text{cm}, \\ b & =AC=10\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $m∠A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 20\sqrt{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 10\cdot 8\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 20\sqrt{2} & =40\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{20\sqrt{2}}{40} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡A & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ m∠A & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/f2/f2a9f5e6149b62b5724de8a46e50e7aac2976ffa2f9f841c64417ffd248fcb88.png)

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Find the measure of $∠A.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=\sqrt{2}\,\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC=\sqrt{6}\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $m∠A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2} & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \cancel{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}} & =\cancel{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 1 & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡A & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ m∠A & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/85/85b13f2236c5f00da34ea71fdbfc967882fa6e66c347f6ef40c0604391a5d68e.png)

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $15{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Find $m∠A.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=5\,\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC=12\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $m∠A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 15 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 12\cdot 5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 15 & =30\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{15}{30} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡A & =\frac{1}{2} \\ m∠A & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
